message.content: {"items":[{"term":"6-7","definition":"A deliberately meaningless number shouted as a comedic interruption, often when someone mentions a number near six or seven.","originContext":"The source associates its spread with a song and a basketball player’s height.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“6-7” is a deliberately meaningless number that gets shouted whenever someone says a number close to six or seven"},{"url":"https://slang.net/blog/2025_top_slang_terms","quote":"This nonsensical phrase was everywhere, including in tweets, TikTok captions, YouTube comments, Discord servers"}]},{"term":"41","definition":"A joke response that works as a contradiction or alternate answer to “6-7.”","originContext":"Described as a cousin term to “6-7.”","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“41,” which functions more like a contradiction or an alternate answer than its own separate joke"}]},{"term":"delulu","definition":"Short for “delusional”; used for an overly optimistic or unrealistic belief, often about a crush, job, or hoped-for outcome.","originContext":"The source traces its spread to K-pop stan culture on Twitter.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Delulu” is short for delusional, and it almost always describes someone’s own overly optimistic or unrealistic belief"}]},{"term":"crashing out","definition":"Having a visible emotional or behavioral meltdown, often triggered by stress or a personal conflict.","originContext":"The source describes it as a slang shift used for a public escalation of private frustration.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"To “crash out,” or to have a “crash out,” means having a visible emotional or behavioral meltdown"}]},{"term":"aura farming","definition":"Deliberately acting or moving to appear effortlessly cool, often in a way that others mock as try-hard.","originContext":"The source links the phrase to sports and gaming clip culture.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Aura farming” describes deliberately acting or moving in a way designed to look effortlessly cool"}]},{"term":"canon event","definition":"An unavoidable, defining moment in someone’s life story.","originContext":"Borrowed from fandom language about what counts as real in a fictional universe, then applied to everyday life.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"A “canon event” is a moment framed as an unavoidable, defining part of someone’s story"}]},{"term":"chopped","definition":"Describes something as unattractive, unappealing, or generally messed up; it can also mean someone has little chance of succeeding.","originContext":"Used in fashion, beauty, roasting, and commentary about someone’s prospects.","sources":[{"url":"https://slang.net/blog/2025_top_slang_terms","quote":"Chopped is slang for something that looks unattractive, unappealing, or generally \"messed up,\" as if it's been badly cut or ruined."},{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"Calling someone or something “chopped” means it looks bad or has no real shot"}]},{"term":"mewing","definition":"A tongue-posture technique that some people believe can sharpen jawline definition.","originContext":"The source says the technique predates its current meme status and its aesthetic claims are unverified.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Mewing” refers to a tongue-posture technique some people believe sharpens jawline definition"}]},{"term":"unc","definition":"A familiar term, usually for a man, used online for someone acting older, more out of touch, or more cautious than their age suggests.","originContext":"The source traces it to Black American English, where it could be affectionate before broader internet use.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Unc” describes someone, usually a man, acting older, more out of touch, or more cautious than his actual age suggests"}]},{"term":"brat","definition":"A label for someone confidently unbothered, somewhat messy, and unapologetically themselves.","originContext":"The source describes a pop-culture-driven shift from the older meaning of a spoiled child.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Brat” now describes someone confidently unbothered, a little messy, and unapologetically themselves"}]},{"term":"biblically accurate","definition":"Describes something strange, overwhelming, or unsettling, referencing depictions of angels drawn as described in scripture.","originContext":"The source connects the usage to a meme sparked by religious-art depictions of angels.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"Calling something “biblically accurate” means it looks strange, overwhelming, or unsettling"}]},{"term":"beige flag","definition":"A personality quirk that is neither a real warning sign nor a positive trait, but is mildly odd or unremarkable.","originContext":"A dating term that extends the red-flag and green-flag framework with a neutral middle category.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"A “beige flag” is a personality quirk that isn’t a genuine warning sign and isn’t a positive trait either"}]},{"term":"NPC energy","definition":"Behavior that seems scripted or makes someone blend into the background, evoking a non-player character in a video game.","originContext":"The source says a livestream trend involving repetitive behavior helped push the phrase beyond gaming.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“NPC energy” describes someone acting like they’re following a script or blending into the background"}]},{"term":"brain rot","definition":"Low-value, low-effort content, or the mentally foggy feeling associated with consuming too much of it.","originContext":"The source describes it as starting as a self-aware joke about scrolling habits and later becoming a descriptor for content.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Brain rot” describes low-value, low-effort content, or the mentally foggy feeling that comes from consuming too much of it"},{"url":"https://slang.net/blog/2025_top_slang_terms","quote":"Brain rot (or \"brainrot\") describes content, media, or experiences that are fun but mind-numbing"}]},{"term":"skibidi","definition":"An absurdist filler word with no fixed meaning.","originContext":"The source roots it in an animated meme series and describes its use as sound- and repetition-driven.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Skibidi” has no fixed meaning and functions as pure absurdist filler"}]},{"term":"glazing","definition":"Excessively praising or flattering someone in a way that feels forced or embarrassing.","originContext":"The source says it spread across TikTok, Twitch, and Discord in the early 2020s.","sources":[{"url":"https://slang.net/blog/2025_top_slang_terms","quote":"Glazing refers to excessively praising or sucking up to someone in a way that feels forced or embarrassing."}]},{"term":"slay","definition":"Used to praise someone’s confidence, style, or ability to do something impressively.","originContext":"The source describes it as a continuing compliment in texts and online comments.","sources":[{"url":"https://slang.net/blog/2025_top_slang_terms","quote":"slay is used to compliment someone's confidence, style, or ability to \"own it.\""}]},{"term":"zesty","definition":"Describes something lively, energetic, or slightly chaotic in an enjoyable way.","originContext":"The source attributes renewed popularity to viral TikTok edits and online commentary.","sources":[{"url":"https://slang.net/blog/2025_top_slang_terms","quote":"Zesty describes something lively, energetic, or slightly chaotic in a fun way."}]},{"term":"mogging","definition":"Outshining or dominating someone, especially in looks, skills, or status.","originContext":"The source associates it with fitness, gaming, and meme communities, where it can signal bragging or playful competition.","sources":[{"url":"https://slang.net/blog/2025_top_slang_terms","quote":"Mogging comes from online culture and refers to outshining or \"dominating\" someone, especially in terms of looks, skills, or status."}]},{"term":"67","definition":"A nonsensical phrase used as a versatile filler or punchline in jokes, references, or online challenges.","originContext":"The source describes it as a viral meme and trend, especially among Gen Alpha.","sources":[{"url":"https://slang.net/blog/2025_top_slang_terms","quote":"This nonsensical phrase was everywhere, including in tweets, TikTok captions, YouTube comments, Discord servers, and meme compilations, and is often used as a versatile filler or punchline"}]}]}
